page: The Vultr vhf-8c-32gb is an instance in the High Frequency Compute family powered by x86_64 Intel processors. The virtual machine provides 8 vCPUs configured across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled on a shared CPU allocation model running at 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX, AES encryption, and BMI2, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Memory allocation is set at 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per thread.

Integrated local storage is provisioned as a 512 GB NVMe SSD, delivering local high-speed disk access directly attached to the instance without requiring separate volume provisioning. No discrete GPU acceleration is included. The instance also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmark data exhibits top-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 41.55 GB/sec and a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3043.43. Geekbench text processing and single-threaded bzip3 decompression also place in the upper quartile.

General computational metrics reflect middle-tier baseline throughput. The instance recorded a multi-core Geekbench score of 7016.0, single-core score of 1827.0, and PassMark CPU score of 16168.89. Uncached memory bandwidth represents a tradeoff, measuring 37.7 GB/sec for reads and 18.84 GB/sec for writes in large 256 MB blocks, which places in the bottom quartile. Similarly, medium-scale local LLM inference yields poor token throughput. Sustained execution shows balanced behavior for static web serving at 9.41 GB/sec and Redis SET operations reaching 13.72 million operations per second.

Balancing 8 vCPUs with 32.0 GB RAM and bundled NVMe capacity offers balanced resource density on shared hardware. This profile aligns with production web serving, continuous integration builds, application backends, Redis caching, and relational databases that benefit from attached fast NVMe storage.
description: The Vultr vhf-8c-32gb is a High Frequency Compute instance delivering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical Intel x86_64 cores operating at 2.0 GHz with hyperthreading on a shared CPU allocation. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, and includes 512 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmarks reveal top-tier single-thread gzip compression speeds of 41.55 GB/sec and strong memory assessment scores, alongside reliable middle-tier Geekbench and Redis transaction results. However, uncached large-block memory bandwidth is comparatively constrained. Lacking dedicated GPU acceleration, the hardware profile represents a dense, balanced configuration suited for medium-scale database servers, CI/CD compilation pipelines, Redis caching clusters, and standard enterprise web application hosting.
